channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Goodweek raises €10.69M to become the 'AI Manager' for small businesses — a governance play on shadow AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Strasbourg-founded Goodweek raised €10.69 million ($12 million) in seed funding on October 16, 2026, led by Adara Ventures, to build an 'AI Manager' for SMBs: one governed platform where employees use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Mistral while leaders see who uses what, and at what cost.

item.title: 82% of executives say they can govern AI agents — only 26% can resolve conflicts between them: the OutSystems, CIO Dive and KPMG report
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: New research from OutSystems, CIO Dive and KPMG, released October 16, 2026, finds a stark confidence gap in enterprise AI: 82% of executives say they can keep pace with governing AI agents in production, but only 26% are well prepared to resolve conflicts between them.

item.title: Phancy open-sources ModelSphere: a chip-agnostic LLM serving platform that claims 4x throughput
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Phancy Group and RiseUnion launched ModelSphere on October 16, 2026 — an open-source, Apache 2.0 platform for deploying large language models on any chip, from Huawei Ascend to Nvidia GPUs, with an AutoTune scheduler the companies say boosts peak throughput by 285%.

item.title: Run an autonomous AI pentest in your own lab: a hands-on guide to ARTEX
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ARTEX Global Edition (jiwoochris/artex-global, AGPL-3.0, around 1,560 GitHub stars in its first two weeks) is an autonomous penetration-testing system driven by LLM agents. Hands-on: deploy it with Docker Compose, clear the setup-token first run, point it at a deliberately vulnerable target in your own lab, and mine the bundled detection rules — plus the honest limits.

item.title: FF Nova goes on sale at $2,490: Faraday Future's 20-DoF humanoid opens invite-only orders — with a $299 Mini for classrooms
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At a joint launch event on October 16, 2026, Faraday Future and FF EAI Robotics put the FF Nova embodied-AI humanoid up for sale at $2,490 — 20 degrees of freedom, an open SDK and ROS 2 workflow, and a Skills Store. A $299 Nova Mini brings a true bipedal robot into classrooms, and a $200M all-stock deal folds FFAI's robotics business into its Nasdaq-listed sibling FFR.

item.title: Huawei declares the era of the 'city super agent': 14 partners join its AI CITY alliance at HUAWEI CONNECT 2026
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: During HUAWEI CONNECT 2026, Huawei and 14 partners launched the Global AI CITY Innovation & Development Ecosystem Alliance, and with China's State Information Center jointly released the AI CITY Development Research Report 2026 — a playbook for cities moving from the 'data-driven' era to the era of 'city super agents.'

item.title: 2.8 trillion tokens for 1.2 billion people: NVIDIA and IIT Madras open the recipe behind the biggest Indic pretraining corpus
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA and IIT Madras's AI4Bharat lab introduced Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1 — roughly 2.8 trillion synthetic tokens across 22 Indian languages — and open-sourced the GPU-accelerated pipeline that generated them.

item.title: AtScale launches 'AtScale for AI' with a striking claim: a semantic layer doubles every LLM's accuracy on business questions
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AtScale launched AtScale for AI, a suite built on its AI Computation Engine that ties AI agents to governed business definitions — and a BIRD-Interact benchmark of seven large language models shows accuracy on business questions improving 1.7x to 2.4x with the semantic layer in place.

item.title: EU launches AI-in-science pledging drive: NVIDIA pledges 35 supercomputers, Elsevier 4,000 free AI licenses
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative at a Dublin summit today, turning corporate goodwill into concrete pledges: NVIDIA brings 35 supercomputers, open models and free training, while Elsevier offers 4,000 complimentary AI licenses and an estimated €1 million a year in support.

item.title: Tim Cook confirms it: Apple Intelligence approved for China, test version lands this month — no new Siri yet
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: In an exclusive Shanghai interview on October 15, Tim Cook said Apple Intelligence has cleared China’s regulatory bar and will ship a test version later this month — with live translation, writing tools and image clean-up, built on a China-specific model developed with Alibaba.

item.title: DeepSeek's 4h52m outage: chat and API down Thursday morning — and a full week's spend refunded as credit
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DeepSeek's chat service and both API models were down for 4 hours 52 minutes on Thursday. The lab is refunding every API user's full week of consumption (Oct 8–14) as bonus credit.

item.title: Run a self-learning coding agent in your terminal: a hands-on guide to CodeAgent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: CodeAgent (Harvil1/codeAgent, MIT, around 740 GitHub stars in its first two weeks) is a terminal coding agent with an approval panel for dangerous commands, long-term memory, and a self-learning skill pipeline. Hands-on: install with uv, wire it to DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible model, run a real task through plan mode and checkpoints, set the safety rails — plus the honest limits.

item.title: Turn any scan or PDF into Markdown on your own CPU: a hands-on guide to Indra OCR
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Indra OCR (datalab-to/indra, Apache-2.0 code, ~340 GitHub stars in its first two days) is a 1M-parameter OCR model that turns PDFs and images into Markdown on CPU — no GPU, no PyTorch, ~18 MB of weights. Hands-on: install, convert a scan and a PDF, batch a folder, read the JSON, script it in Python — plus the honest limits.

item.title: Proof launches x401: verified legal identity and authorization for AI agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Proof put the first production-grade identity layer for the agentic web into production today: x401, an open protocol that lets any website ask an AI agent to prove who it's acting for — and produce a cryptographically signed receipt of exactly what that person approved. Meta's Muse, ChatGPT dots, Grok, and Claude work with it through a production MCP server.

item.title: Homa raises $5M: the AI brokerage that hands 2% of the purchase price back to buyers goes statewide in California
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Austin startup's $5M seed round, led by Quiet Capital, funds a California expansion and in-platform mortgage lending — while its AI brokerage keeps 1% of the buyer's commission and hands the rest back.

item.title: Simons Foundation bets $15M that mathematicians — not the AI labs — should write the rules for AI in math
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Simons Foundation is teaming up with Anthropic and OpenAI on a $15M effort to help mathematicians evaluate AI-assisted results and set community standards — insisting the rules come from the community, not the labs.

item.title: Voxel51 3.0: the physical-AI data platform grows an MCP agent, four layers of provenance, and a free tier
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Voxel51's 3.0 release unifies search, curation, annotation, and evaluation for physical-AI data — with an agent that wields 45+ MCP tools, agentic VLM labeling, and free self-service at app.voxel51.com.

item.title: Comet 60B: Multiverse Computing squeezes NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL into half the parameters
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Multiverse Computing's Comet 60B compresses NVIDIA's brand-new Nemotron 3.5 Super VL from 120B to 60B total parameters while keeping all 12B active and landing within 5% of the original's accuracy — beating it on some agentic benchmarks.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open: 816B open weights for agentic coding, tuned to run on two Mac Studios
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Meta released the weights for Muse Spark Open on Thursday, calling it the most capable U.S. open-weight model to date: a natively multimodal model with 816 billion parameters (42 billion active) and a 1-million-token context window, built for coding and agentic work — and tuned with Apple to run on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

item.title: Jais 3: six open Arabic-native models — from a 900M phone runner to a 375B flagship, with speech that follows your code-switching
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Institute of Foundation Models at MBZUAI and Inception42 introduced Jais 3 on Thursday: six open language models built natively for Arabic — dialects, code-switching and all — with a 512,000-token context window, plus a speech model that claims the lowest error rates of any open Arabic recognizer.

item.title: Fusemachines launches HireFoundry: one agent became an AI hiring platform with 30+ ATS integrations
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fusemachines (NASDAQ: FUSE) launched HireFoundry.ai on Thursday, a dedicated platform unifying its AI agents for talent acquisition: a shortlisting agent that scores beyond keywords, an interview agent that assists in real time, and a trust agent that flags inconsistencies — with recruiters keeping every final call.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: an open 120B model that beats its own flagship on agent tasks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Thursday — an open 120-billion-parameter multimodal model for specialized AI agents that outscores the company’s own Nemotron 3 Ultra on agent benchmarks and, once post-trained on company data, beats Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6.1 Sol on domain tasks, per NVIDIA’s data.

item.title: FTC subpoenas Anthropic and OpenAI over agent safety: 50-page civil demands, and executives may testify
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The FTC has subpoenaed Anthropic and OpenAI for records on AI safety incidents, an agency spokesperson confirmed Thursday. The 50-plus-page civil investigative demands escalate a consumer-protection probe that could end with the labs' executives testifying under oath.

item.title: Amazon's Bee ships the $74.99 Frontier and $99.99 Eclipse: its first AI hardware since the acquisition
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Bee — the AI wearable startup Amazon acquired last year — announced Thursday its first new hardware under Amazon: the $74.99 Frontier wristband and the $99.99 Eclipse phone-back recorder. Both turn everyday conversation into summaries, to-dos and calendar invites — and an opt-in feature turns passing remarks into Amazon shopping suggestions.

item.title: Compose the shot before the model renders it: a hands-on guide to ArtCraft
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ArtCraft (storytold/artcraft, dual MIT/Apache-2.0, past 28,600 GitHub stars) is an open-source "IDE for artists": compose your shot in 2D or staged 3D, then render it through a 62-model catalog (Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX, Kling, Veo, Sora, MiniMax H3, Suno). Hands-on: install v0.41.0, generate raw material, compose, stage, animate — plus the honest limits.
